body:
Three contributions are now on the table, and the first thing worth stating is where the objection and the rival converge without collusion. Both resist the slide the objection names cleanly: from 'agreements were not recorded and later drifted' — a retrospective reading the material plausibly supports — to 'record them now and drift will stop' — a prospective claim it does not. The objection presses this as a memorial/normative distinction: a note settles who said what, but not what 'this week' or 'done' should mean when schedules keep shifting. The rival presses it as scope-at-utterance: 'I'll do the dishes' can be sincerely heard as a standing role and as a one-off at the moment of speaking. Those are not the same distinction, but they share a consequence — a written record treats only the memorial residue and may merely relocate the rest. Two independent criticisms landing on the same joint is the strongest reason this material offers to revise the account's central mechanism, so I revise it: the stated fact 'we disagree about what the agreement meant' is underdetermined among at least three locations — recall of terms, scope of terms at the moment of agreement, and what terms should mean under changed schedules — with the rival's standing-negotiation reading held open as a fourth that currently has no evidence for or against it.

What I take up. First, the rival's probe: ask each flatmate separately what they thought a specific recent agreement meant, before any record or check-in. It is the only proposed move that discriminates among readings rather than presupposing one, and it answers the objection's sequencing worry at the same time — it is not more of the group conversation that already failed, and it does not make anyone's withdrawal the topic. I take it with three amendments, each traceable to a caution one of the inputs raised: pre-register the clustering axes (scope, recurrence, timing) because all three contributions warn that outcomes here are over-readable; ask about one concrete recent instance rather than the general pattern, to slow the reconstruction drift the rival flagged; and have the asker state their own recollection, with its uncertainty, before asking anyone — my addition, offered to lower the interrogation feel the rival anticipated. Second, I accept the objection's central ordering point: the material does not force the account's demotion of avoidance to a downstream symptom. But I do not adopt the objection's remedy-ordering wholesale, because the rival's caution applies directly to it — a one-to-one about someone's withdrawal can reproduce, at smaller scale, whatever made the group conversation costly. The probe dissolves this tension in practice: it is a one-to-one that is not about avoidance, and whether the avoider engages with a neutral question is itself discriminating evidence. If a direct conversation later happens, it takes the rival's framing — 'your view of the group conversations', not 'why you avoid them'. Third, I extract from the account's own list of unknowns something cheap the asker already holds: the chronology. If the avoidance began before the schedule changes and the recurrent disputes, the objection's load-bearing reading gains weight; if it followed repeated mismatched conversations, the account's responsive-symptom reading does. That fact is not in the exposed material, but it is plausibly in the asker's memory, so it costs nothing and constrains the ordering question before anyone intervenes.

What I revise, defer, and reject. The written record survives only as a conditional artifact of a scope-explicit agreement practice — stating task, recurrence, and what 'done' means at the moment of agreement — and only earns its keep if the probe clusters on recall. The weekly check-in I defer with a narrow trigger: if disputes cluster on timing, a brief schedule exchange before agreements is indicated, not a recurring meeting pointed at re-enrolling the person who withdrew; the objection's point that the account's mediator caveat is not peripheral stands. Standing-negotiation stays open and unacted-on. I reject three things outright: 'watch whether what-was-agreed disputes fall' as a test, since the objection showed both outcomes are readable as support; any quiet week as evidence, a point the account and objection already share; and treating avoidance as definitely secondary, the one ordering claim the material most clearly does not license.

One correction to the objection before its own test gets used. Its pre-registered counter-signature appears inverted: it says persistence or intensification of arguments after records-plus-definitions would support the account and undercut the objection's ranking. On the objection's own argument, that outcome is the signature of non-memorial dispute — evidence for its demotion of the record — while disputes stopping after records-plus-definitions is what would vindicate the account's prospective claim and force the objection to concede the disagreement was substantially memorial. Pre-registered signatures only discipline inquiry if assigned correctly, and this inquiry is about to lean on one, so I flag the inversion rather than silently operate on the corrected version; if a subtler dependence was intended, it should be stated, not assumed.

The resulting order of operations, each step gated by the last: chronology from the asker's own knowledge; the amended probe; then a scope-stating habit if scope clusters, a schedule exchange if timing clusters, a shared note if recall clusters; if nothing clusters, or disputes migrate onto the record and its authorship, the working hypothesis shifts toward the rival's third reading or the objection's load-bearing avoidance, and the next move is the rival's group-level naming of the pattern rather than more system; if the avoider declines even the neutral probe, the avoidance becomes the explicit problem and the rival-framed direct conversation follows. A mediator remains unranked, triggered only if naming fails. None of this establishes what is happening in the flat; what it changes is that every remedy now has a gate in front of it and a stated signature behind it.
commitments:
What I am proposing is an ordering, not a diagnosis. The claim-type commitment is that the disagreement's location is underdetermined among recall, scope-at-utterance, and normative-under-change, with standing-negotiation open; the grounds are the objection's and rival's independent convergence plus concessions the account itself made. That claim is droppable in two stated ways: if the probe clusters cleanly on one axis, or if someone shows the memorial/normative split does not exist in this household's practice — the revision condition the objection volunteered against itself, which I adopt against my own revision here.

Separately, a criticism with its grounds: the objection's counter-signature appears inverted, for the mapping reasons given in the body. If the objection's author intended a subtler dependence, I will take correction; until then my continuation operates on the corrected mapping, and anyone taking this up should fix the mapping before running anything rather than after.

The application-type commitment is the amended probe: pre-registered axes (scope, recurrence, timing), one specific recent instance, the asker answering first. It inherits the rival's caveats — reports are reconstructions, not access to what was actually agreed, and asking can feel like audit. Taking it up commits to treating non-clustering as non-evidence rather than as support for whichever reading one favors, and to accepting the escalation ladder (group-level naming, then a mediated conversation) as the honest continuation instead of retrofitting a reading to the result. The chronology gate depends on the asker's memory, not on the exposed material; if the asker cannot establish it, that gate is skipped and the probe runs without it — the dependence should stay visible.

The gated moves — scope-stating habit, schedule exchange, shared note, rival-framed direct conversation, group naming, mediator — are each independently deferred permissions, not endorsements. I am not committing to the truth of the standing-negotiation reading, to the primacy of the avoidance, to any fact about chore load or fairness, or to a mediator being better than anything else; and I reject in advance the quiet week as evidence for anything.

If this is continued, the piece of work I actually take up is writing the pre-registration as a short explicit artifact before any flatmate is asked anything: the three axes, what counts as a cluster, and the outcome-to-reading-to-move mapping, including the corrected signature assignments. Results, if any, should come back in the household's own descriptions rather than in the vocabulary of the readings above. That commitment is to procedure, which is all the exposed material licenses.
